title: Melt. Freeze. Prove.
youtubeTitle: Melt and Freeze a Hardware Circuit — What HELUT Actually Proves
description: HELUT's melt/freeze path is shown as implemented, and the join it used to be missing is now closed. Fixed-topology LUT truth tables are lifted from binary entries to Float32 values, selected LUTs are searched with evolutionary mutation and crossover, and a threshold returns the mutable region to discrete tables when target fitness is preserved. The searched result is then emitted, re-synthesized by Yosys, and proven equivalent to a behavioural Verilog reference by SAT (miter -equiv + minisat over the post-abc -lut 6 artifact); corrupting one discovered entry yields a counterexample. The cold open is a live run: on an 8-bit adder with 16 LUTs, a 2-LUT melt trained on 64 of 65,536 rows (0.10%) is formally proven over all 65,536 assignments, and the erased baseline is REFUTED on every row. A low-budget failure control is shown too: melting 8 of 8 LUTs at 120 generations returns a fully binary, zero-fractional, still-incorrect circuit at fitness -16; the same fixture proves at 500 generations, so this is budget sensitivity rather than a hard method frontier. Sequential repair is also shown live: a transition behind one DFF is erased, rediscovered as q_next = q XOR x, and proven by post-ABC equiv_induct over every matched Boolean state and all enable/reset/input combinations, with a reset-to-divergence counterexample when one discovered INIT bit is flipped. Open: arbitrary topology, convergence guarantees, coupled or multi-DFF repair, and any area or depth win over Yosys/ABC (6 LUTs vs 6). An archived M4 targeted-melt failure remains visible. Epoch C70.

scenes.headline: Melt. Freeze. Prove.
scenes.subhead: Continuous truth tables are useful only if the discrete circuit survives.
scenes.voiceover: The search never saw 65,472 of those input rows, and the proof covers them anyway. That is the result worth sitting with, so here is the machinery behind it. A lookup table in HELUT holds truth-table entries that are normally exact zeros and ones. Melting lets selected entries become floating-point values in between, so a search can move them. Freezing pushes them back to exact binary. Proving means handing the resulting discrete circuit to a tool that had no part in the search and letting it try to break the result. This episode shows the controlled pass, the checker that catches corruption, a low-budget failure control, and the exact sentence where a general claim would outrun the evidence.

scenes.label: LIVE RUN · recorded 2026-09-05 · prebuilt test bundle · not a replay
scenes.voiceover: Watch the rows column. That is an 8-bit adder: 16 lookup tables and 65,536 possible inputs. Two tables are erased. The repair search sees only 64 rows: 0.10 percent. It finds the missing logic, then Yosys re-synthesizes the result and SAT proves equivalence to behavioural addition across all 65,536 assignments. The erased baseline is REFUTED, so the circuit was genuinely broken. On this fixture, search did not enumerate the domain and the independent proof covers unseen rows. One fixture is not an asymptotic complexity result. Second screen, the failure control. Erase 2 of 8 tables and it proves. 4, it proves. 6, it proves. Erase all 8 at this 120-generation budget and it returns fully binary but wrong, fitness -16. That is not where the method stops: the same fixture proves at 500 generations in episode 3's live gate. Binarity is not correctness, and search budget matters.

scenes.headline: Topology stays fixed; INIT values move
scenes.subhead: 64 Float32 entries per LUT6 · frozen or mutable by block
scenes.voiceover: What melts is the INIT table inside a lookup-table block. INIT is the Verilog parameter that spells out a table's truth values, and TensorLUT pads every supported table to 64 Float32 entries, six inputs being the widest cell it accepts. Evaluation uses the multilinear extension: each of the 64 entries is weighted by how strongly the inputs point at its corner of the cube. Feed it exact zeros and ones and only one weight is nonzero, so it returns the same entry Boolean logic would. Feed it fractions and it interpolates between corners. A freeze mask then picks which whole blocks mutation may touch. Wires, connections, lookup-table count, and flip-flop count never move, because the genome is nothing but INIT floats. No operator exists that could move them. That matters, because a phrase like genetic hardware implies topology search. This is narrower: evolutionary search over truth-table parameters on a fixed graph. Useful for inverse design or targeted repair. Not structural logic synthesis.

scenes.kicker: The microscope · small enough to exhaust
scenes.headline: A four-LUT two-bit adder
scenes.subhead: 4 inputs · 3 outputs · 16 complete rows · 2 logic levels
scenes.voiceover: The strongest controlled example is deliberately tiny. A two-bit adder built from four lookup tables, scheduled in two execution levels, meaning two rounds of evaluation where everything inside a round can be computed at once. Four primary input bits, three output bits, so the entire combinational domain is 16 assignments. The first level computes the low sum with XOR and the low carry with AND. The second level combines the two upper input bits with that carry. Because every possible input fits on one page, comparing all 16 rows later is exhaustive for this function rather than a sample. Small does not mean weak evidence here. It means the word proof can be used literally.

scenes.kicker: Freeze what is known · erase what is not
scenes.headline: Two LUTs frozen, two LUTs melted
scenes.subhead: 128 mutable floats wiped to 0.5 · 128 frozen floats preserved
scenes.voiceover: The targeted experiment freezes the two low-bit tables and lets only the two carry-stage tables move. 64 entries each, so the mutable region is 128 floats, and every one of them is wiped to 0.5: maximally undecided under this representation. The frozen blocks keep their original binary tables byte for byte, and that is the first falsifiable gate. If mutation or crossover disturbs a single frozen entry, the test fails. It is worth being precise about what is being asked here. The carry-stage tables were declared as all zeros to begin with, so there is no correct answer hiding underneath the wipe. The search has to discover the carry logic, not remember it, while the rest of the circuit stays fixed.

scenes.headline: Mutation, crossover, target error, binarity pressure
scenes.voiceover: The implemented search is evolutionary, not gradient descent. 48 chromosomes, each one a full copy of the lookup-table entries. Sparse Gaussian mutation nudges mutable values, occasional jumps land exactly on zero or one, and crossover swaps whole 64-entry blocks between parents. The objective has two terms. The first is what the code calls crypto fitness: the negative sum of squared output error, so zero is perfect and everything else is worse. The second is a binarity penalty, the sum of w times one minus w over every mutable entry, which is zero at zero and at one and largest at one half. Its lambda weight sits at nothing for the first tenth of the run and then ramps up, so the search fits the target first and feels pressure toward binary tables later. The two-bit control pins all of it: 120 generations, seed 0x7A6E17, a lambda ceiling of 12, and one binary polish attempt at the end.

scenes.kicker: Thresholding is a proposal, not a proof
scenes.headline: Snap at 0.5, then score again
scenes.subhead: Accept only if hard target fitness stays within 0.001
scenes.voiceover: Polish proposes a discrete chromosome by thresholding each mutable entry at 0.5. Below becomes zero, at or above becomes one. HELUT then re-scores that hard version against the same target and accepts it only if hard crypto fitness comes out no more than 0.001 worse than the soft version it would replace. That is a real safety gate, and it deserves an accurate name. It is a check against this experiment's target, not a theorem about equivalence. Zero fractional entries tells you the result is discrete. On its own it tells you nothing about whether the result is right.

scenes.label: LIVE RUN · recorded 2026-09-05 · prebuilt test bundle · not a replay
scenes.voiceover: Two gates, both live. First the freeze mask: 6 tests, zero failures, and the one that matters is the targeted melt, which discovers the carry logic while the known tables stay byte-identical. If mutation touched a single frozen entry that test fails. Second gate, the hardware round trip. The circuit is emitted as Verilog, handed to Yosys, mapped by ABC, reloaded, and compared: 48 output bits over all 16 inputs. Every claim here has a matching negative control, because a gate that cannot fail is decoration. Corrupt one table, 4 mismatches. Corrupt a discovered entry, 3 of 48. Now read the two SEQUENTIAL lines, because those are new. A state transition behind a flip-flop was erased, rediscovered as q-next equals q XOR x, and proven by induction over every matched state and every enable and reset combination. Flip one discovered bit and induction refuses, handing back a reset-to-divergence trace. That is repair with state.

scenes.headline: Emit → Yosys → reload → exhaust all rows
scenes.subhead: 48 output bits agree · corrupted INIT observed: 4 mismatches
scenes.voiceover: An older identity-round-trip test closes the emitter and checker loop. It takes the unmutated four-table adder, emits it as six-input LUT Verilog, hands the file to Yosys, maps it with ABC, writes a fresh JSON netlist, reloads that netlist, and compares three outputs across all 16 inputs. 48 output bits agree. Flip one INIT entry and today's run reports 4 mismatches; the assertion only requires at least one, so four is observed rather than pinned. This older receipt did not join search to proof. The newer searched-elite test now does: search the erased tables, emit the discovered result, re-synthesize it, prove the full domain, then flip one discovered entry and demand a counterexample.

scenes.kicker: The failure stays in the ledger
scenes.headline: A larger targeted melt did not freeze
scenes.subhead: 925 LUT · 49 DFF · 16 mutable · 118 entries still fractional
scenes.voiceover: The archived M4 run is the counterweight, and it used a different configuration from the two-bit control: population 16, lambda ceiling 10, 150 generations of exploring followed by 250 of squeezing. Exploring means chasing target fitness with the binarity penalty switched off. Squeezing means turning that penalty up to force the entries binary. The graph held 925 lookup tables and 49 flip-flops, 16 tables mutable and 909 frozen. Exploring worked: sampled fitness climbed from -4.25 to -1.9. Squeezing did not. It finished with 118 entries still non-binary and target fitness back down at -4.94. A Verilog file came out anyway, because the emitter thresholds whatever it is handed. No equivalence check ever said that file was correct, so this is a failure, not a near-success parked behind an artifact path. The project's answer was to stop searching for plugboard reciprocity in truth-table entries and enforce it structurally instead.

scenes.headline: HELUT and ABC optimize different things
scenes.subhead: Different knob, and the combined flow has now been measured
scenes.voiceover: So how does this compare with logic simplification as it already exists? Yosys and ABC rewrite Boolean structure. They remove redundancy, merge cells, map to a target library, and trade depth against area. The HELUT search holds structure still and changes lookup-table values to fit a target while pushing them toward binary. Its objective carries no area term, no depth term, and no timing or power term. So the two are not doing the same job. The fair question is what happens when you run the combined flow: discover a new discrete function on fixed topology, emit it, then let ABC strip whatever redundancy that creates, and hand both the original and the discovered circuit to the same mapper. That flow has now run end to end on six circuits. The next screen is its receipt, and it is not the answer a promoter would want.

scenes.label: PRESERVED RECEIPT · identical abc -lut 6 on both sides · measured null
scenes.voiceover: One flow, printed at the top, runs identically on both sides: read the LUT6 model, flatten, optimize, techmap, then abc -lut 6, then check. Area is the mapped lookup-table count. Depth is the worst output cone. Proof is a miter and a SAT solve against independent behavioural Verilog. Before mapping, the search does real work. The 8-bit adder falls from 41 tables to 16. The multiplexer halves. The multiplier drops from 18 to 6. If I stopped the screen there, I could sell you a simplifier. Then the same recipe maps both sides, and the columns land on top of each other. 14 against 14. Three against three. Six against six. Across six circuits and three seeds, that is 18 results: zero wins, 18 ties, zero losses on count, and the same on depth. Every retained finalist was proved. The receipt calls it an honest null, because the search removed redundant cones and ABC removed the same redundancy. The boundary line is on screen too: these are mapping proxies, not area, delay, frequency, or power.

scenes.headline: What melt/freeze proves today
scenes.subhead: Representation: yes. Rediscovery: yes. End-to-end re-proof: yes. Simplification: measured null.
scenes.voiceover: Four rows, then. One: a Yosys lookup-table graph can be lifted into continuous truth-table parameters and evaluated on Metal. Two: a freeze mask protects known tables while a deterministic evolutionary search discovers an acceptable discrete solution. Three: TensorLUT Verilog survives Yosys re-synthesis and exhaustive checking, and the checker catches a one-bit corruption. Four, and this is the row that changed: those two lanes are joined now. A searched elite is emitted, re-synthesized by Yosys, and proven by SAT against behavioural addition over the whole input space; corrupting one discovered entry produces a counterexample instead of a pass. A fifth row is sequential repair: one transition behind one flip-flop is rediscovered and proven by induction, with a concrete divergence trace on corruption. One flip-flop is not a processor. Still open are arbitrary topologies, convergence guarantees, coupled or multi-flip-flop repair, and general simplification. There is no area or depth win over ABC, and that is now measured rather than assumed: six circuits, 18 seed results, zero wins, 18 ties, zero losses under one identical mapping recipe. Melt and freeze is real and re-provable end to end, but its current evidence remains fixture-scoped.
